why: Khalid, 2026-10-21: a puller that runs before its source publishes for the day shows yesterday's print for a whole day; each provider is a pinned writer that fires at its publication time, and its pullers move later inside their own window (scripts/pipeline_order.py, pass 3). Pulls of one provider are spread so that no more than slot_max of them start on the same minute (rate limits: FRED 120 req/min per key, ECB/SEC/government portals throttle bursts, the 14:00 UTC FMP 429 storm of 2026-09-15).
time_note: UTC times are the winter ones (EST / CET), so they hold all year: in summer the print is an hour earlier and the margin grows from 30 to 90 minutes.

FRED.what: H.15 daily rates, yields, FX, commodities (16:15 ET): an engine that pulls any daily series is freshest in the US morning, so only the evening print aligns it

FRED macro.what: 08:30 ET economic releases (payrolls, CPI, claims ...) posted to FRED within minutes: engines that pull no daily series

SEC EDGAR.what: filings accepted until 22:00 ET; the day's index is complete after

Cboe.what: end-of-day index and settlement values (16:15 ET)

FINRA.what: Reg SHO daily short volume files, US evening

EIA.what: weekly petroleum (Wed) and natural gas (Thu) 10:30 ET

not_aligned.FMP: no fixed daily print (statements and calendars update through the day; end-of-day prices in the evening) - spread only
not_aligned.Polygon/Massive: end-of-day aggregates land after the close; the intraday lane (config/intraday-lane.json) is the freshness path - spread only
not_aligned.CFTC: weekly (Friday 15:30 ET); a daily puller gets the new file on its first run after Friday evening
